chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Musawwimin' (Marked/Signs). He said: 'The turbans. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wore a turban and let it hang from in front of him and from behind him, and Jibraeel (peace be upon him) wore a turban and let it hang from in front of him and from behind him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Musawwimin' in the Quran according to Shia hadith, and how did the Prophet wear his turban?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Quranic term 'Musawwimin' by linking it to the specific sartorial practice of wearing a turban with ends hanging front and back, a style attributed to both the Prophet Muhammad and the Angel Jibraeel. It highlights the concept of 'takhassus' (distinctive identification) in Shia jurisprudence, where physical appearance serves as a divine sign, and underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition through angelic precedent.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Abu Hamman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [3:125] marked Angels. Heasws said: ‘The turbans which Rasool-Allahsaww wore, so hesaww let it loose from in front of himsaww, and from behind himsaww, and Jibraeelas wore it letting it loose from in front of himas and from behind himas’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Hammam who has said the following: “This is about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘marked angels.’ [3:125] Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that it is a reference to turbans.

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, wore a turban and hanged down one end on his front side and the other end down his backside. Jibril wore a turban and hanged down one end on his front side and the other end down his back.’”
